- **The real layout of the world (continents, oceans, sea routes)** [`world_geography`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/world_geography.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The Earth is a sphere with one inhabited landmass. Marco Polo and friars describe Cathay; Pegolotti gives the road from Tana. Ptolemy's Geography is unknown. No America, no southern Africa. Local: Pegolotti's Pratica della mercatura (route to Cathay); Tuscan copies of Marco Polo's Milione; Boccaccio's note on the Canaries voyage of 1341. Elsewhere: Genoa and Majorca, charts that now show the Canaries; India, the Florentine friar Giovanni de' Marignolli returning from the Khan's court; Cairo and Tabriz, Arabic geography.

- **Magnetic compass** [`magnetic_compass`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/magnetic_compass.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. The pivoted needle with a wind-rose card has been common on Mediterranean ships for about a generation. The needle is said to seek the pole star or northern lodestone mountains. Elsewhere: Genoa, Venice, Amalfi, Majorca: compass makers; Pisa and Porto Pisano: ship chandlers.

The needle is believed to point true north. Chart makers have unknowingly built the offset into their charts. Elsewhere: China, variation recorded since the 11th century.
